Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl (an archived capture whose archive and WARC location are recorded) has a heading naming this order number, a date and subject agreeing with the held text, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the clause-drafts copy. EO 7431 (August 17, 1936), read in full, exempts George C. Havenner, liaison officer, Government Printing Office, from section 204 of the Act of June 30, 1932 and continues the employee in the service until October 1, 1937. The order states that he will reach the retirement age 'during the month of September, 1936'. Identity: number, date, person and title agree across the APP page record, the census register and the WPA 1944 numbered list. Later orders naming the same employee are held and added to this packet as source-supplement excerpts: EO 7704 (September 10, 1937) recites that Havenner 'was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 7431 of August 17, 1936' and further exempts him until October 1, 1938. Each is recorded as a later event on the clause (clauses.csv). Extension reading, decided on the texts: each later order is a new exercise of the section 204 proviso with its own period. None says that this order 'is amended' or alters its date; each recites the earlier exemption as a past grant ('who was exempted ... by Executive Order No. ...') and grants a further exemption 'until' a new date. The strike-and-insert ruling does not apply because nothing is struck or inserted. So this order's own command ended on its own stated date, inclusive (exclusive alternative: ended when that day began), and each later order is recorded as a later event naming the same employee; the employee's exempt status continued without a gap under the later orders. The alternative reading, that the later orders prolonged this order's command, would put its first end at 1938-10-01 (inclusive); the texts do not support it, because no later order operates on this order's text. Legal reading: a time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1937-10-01, inclusive (exclusive alternative: it stopped when that day began). The census, WPA and full-text name searches found no further order naming this employee beyond those listed. Searches made on 2026-10-28: census register titles (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) and the WPA 1944 numbered list (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv, whitespace-insensitive) for the employee's surname among compulsory-retirement orders, and a full-text search of every held order text under jobs/*/output/texts for the employee's name. The machine USC and eCFR citation searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not relied on alone. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. Held texts of later exemptions show the President still granting exemptions under section 204 after this date (for example EO 7704 of September 10, 1937, running to October 1, 1938, and EO 7725 of October 12, 1937, running to November 1, 1938), which corroborates that the statutory scheme ran through the stated date.

Executive Order

EXEMPTION OF WILLIAM T. MarsSHALL FrRoM COMPULSORY RETIREMENT
FoR AGE

WHEREAS section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S. C.,
sec. 7158), provides:

“On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch
or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the
District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for auto-
matic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in
such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary:
Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions
of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *”;

AND WHEREAS the public interest requires that William T. Marshall, office-
man, Federal Emergency Administration of Public Works, who was exempted from
compulsory retirement for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 7420 of July
20, 1936, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in
the service until August 1, 1938;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me
by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt William T. Marshall from the provisions

thereof and continue him in the service until August 1, 1938.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT
Tae Waite Hovse,
June 8, 1937.

[No. 7629]
